title: Whistleblower alleges serious flaws in new mail voting system
seoTitle: Whistleblower alleges serious flaws in new mail voting.
subtitle: An anonymous federal employee revealed technical and operational problems in the new voting portal.
excerpt: An anonymous whistleblower said the new U.S. mail‑in voting system has serious flaws that could delay thousands of ballots.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
An anonymous federal employee filed a complaint warning of potentially catastrophic problems in the Postal Service's new system for handling mail‑in voting ballots. The complaint was made public and sent to Senator Richard Blumenthal, sparking debate over the integrity and operability of the process for upcoming elections.

The alert about the new voting system

According to the complaint filed by an anonymous federal employee and represented by Whistleblower Aid, the new online portal developed by the Postal Service to house voter information and ballots is defective and was not sufficiently tested. The development process was described as rushed and chaotic, built in a timeframe far shorter than would normally be required.

Technical issues in ballot verification

The document notes that the system has significant operational flaws that could prevent the delivery of large numbers of ballots to voters. The verification policy states that if a single barcode in a large batch fails to read or match the portal, the entire batch will be rejected and returned to state election officials to restart the process.

Violation of court orders

The complaint also accuses the agency of violating court orders by continuing work on the implementation of the executive order signed by President Donald Trump. Postal workers allegedly resumed work on the portal even after federal judges blocked the execution of the measures.

Reactions and questioning in the Senate

Senator Richard Blumenthal questioned USPS Director‑General David Steiner about the platform's development and said the system was designed to make voting harder for millions of people. Election‑law experts also expressed concerns that the new rules create unnecessary barriers and jeopardize the vote of a significant portion of the electorate.

With information from CBS News, NBC News.
